Facts: Ashoka, the grandson of Chandragupta Maurya, ascended the throne of the Mauryan Empire around 268 BCE.
The Kalinga War, fought between the Mauryan Empire under Ashoka and the state of Kalinga, led to massive bloodshed and loss of life. It deeply impacted Ashoka, leading him to embrace Buddhism.
Following the Kalinga War, Ashoka converted to Buddhism and vowed to lead by principles of peace and non-violence.
Ashoka inscribed his policies and moral guidelines on rocks and pillars across his empire, known as the Edicts of Ashoka, which promoted ethical governance and Dharma.
Ashoka sent Buddhist missionaries to various regions, including Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia, to spread the teachings of Buddhism.
